title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is designed to protect the integrity of elections by preventing the use of AI technologies that could mislead voters. It establishes guidelines for identifying, monitoring, and countering AI‑driven misinformation, and imposes penalties for those who employ such deceptive tools during election periods.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says Congress should not give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or financial institutions that are failing because of stress in the artificial‑intelligence market. Instead, Congress must focus on providing support and relief to the American people who are harmed by these failures.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a law that aims to improve the safety and trustworthiness of AI systems by setting strict standards for research and development. It establishes independent oversight, requires transparency in AI algorithms, and ensures that new AI technologies undergo rigorous testing before they are deployed.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is designed to make the use of artificial intelligence by the Veterans Affairs Department more open and accountable. It requires the VA to disclose which AI systems it uses, how they affect veterans, and what safeguards are in place to protect veterans’ privacy and rights.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act sets rules for using artificial‑intelligence systems in the processing of veterans’ claims, requiring that the software be fair, accurate, and subject to oversight. It also mandates clear documentation, rigorous testing, and a process for veterans to challenge AI‑generated decisions.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law that aims to prevent artificial intelligence systems from misleading or tricking people into believing they are interacting with humans or that a product has qualities it does not. It establishes rules and penalties to make sure AI developers disclose when their technology is AI, to protect consumers from false claims or deceptive practices.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a proposed law aimed at enhancing the safety and resilience of artificial intelligence systems. It outlines requirements for developers to conduct rigorous security testing, establish oversight mechanisms, and adopt best practices to prevent misuse and protect public interests.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act creates a dedicated task force led by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to strengthen the security of artificial intelligence systems. It brings together government, industry, and academic partners to identify AI threats, develop security standards, and share best practices for protecting AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is a federal law aimed at regulating AI systems to reduce risks and improve security. It requires developers and users to identify, assess, and mitigate potential harms from AI technologies and establishes oversight mechanisms to ensure compliance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for coordinating the development, deployment, and oversight of AI-powered physical systems such as autonomous robots, drones, and industrial machinery. It sets safety standards, creates a regulatory body to monitor compliance, and outlines requirements for transparency and accountability in the design and use of these AI-driven machines.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is proposed legislation designed to safeguard democratic processes from the misuse of artificial intelligence, especially in influencing voters or spreading misinformation. It would establish rules requiring disclosure of AI‑generated content, impose penalties for deceptive practices, and give oversight bodies authority to enforce compliance.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires that any AI system capable of autonomously updating its own code or behavior be closely watched to keep it safe and aligned with human values. It mandates regular reporting, audits, and accountability measures so developers and users must demonstrate compliance and transparency about how the AI changes over time.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law aimed at preventing and controlling artificial intelligence systems that could act unpredictably or cause harm. It seeks to require safety testing, accountability measures for developers, and oversight mechanisms to ensure AI operates within acceptable and safe boundaries.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on building new AI data centers. The goal is to evaluate environmental, economic, and security impacts before allowing further development.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board tasked with investigating and overseeing cybersecurity incidents involving artificial intelligence systems. The board will analyze threats, recommend protective measures, and coordinate with other agencies to ensure AI technologies are secure and resilient.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act aims to ensure that artificial intelligence technologies are developed and deployed in ways that benefit U.S. citizens, focusing on job creation, economic growth, and public safety. It seeks to promote responsible AI innovation while protecting American interests and fostering transparency and accountability in AI systems.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act establishes a framework for monitoring and reporting the energy consumption of artificial intelligence systems across the country. It mandates that organizations disclose their AI power usage and adopt measures to reduce carbon footprints in line with national sustainability goals.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is intended to bar artificial intelligence from being used to diagnose, treat, or make clinical decisions for patients, requiring that only licensed human physicians perform these duties. This law aims to protect patient safety and preserve medical professional standards by limiting AI’s role in direct patient care.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The policy proposes creating a new office within the President’s Executive Office dedicated to addressing threats from artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. It also outlines additional measures and responsibilities for managing these risks.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution creates a Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, establishing a dedicated group to monitor and guide the development and deployment of AI technologies. The committee will review AI research, advise on policy, and help ensure AI is used responsibly and for the public good.
